title: POC weekly sync - reliability incident follow-up
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on last week's reliability incident (timeouts and 5xxs) during a heavy test run. We reviewed logs, agreed on short-term mitigations (increase retries with jitter, temporary routing to dedicated pool), action items for deeper RCA (trace sampling, kernel-level metrics), and set a follow-up load test and remediation timeline.
topics: dedicated vs hosted routing during peak
next steps for RCA and mitigations
next_steps: Redwood to share filtered server logs and sampled traces for 5xx windows - Priya to upload by 2026-03-06
Customer to run controlled load test (script v2) in staging and share results - Victor to run by 2026-03-09
Agree temporary routing policy to dedicated pool for critical routes - Alex will propose config change by 2026-03-06
Schedule 1-hour deep-dive with kernel/runtime team if RCA needs kernel tuning - tentatively 2026-03-10
action_items: Priya (Redwood SE) - aggregate and redact request/response examples for 5xx windows and upload to secure share - due 2026-03-06
Alex (Redwood AE) - propose temporary routing and retry/backoff config for mitigation and send PR to customer by 2026-03-06
Tom (Aurora SRE) - provide load script parameters and baseline traffic patterns used during the incident - due 2026-03-05
Victor (Aurora) - run controlled staging load test and post metrics (p95/p99 latency, error rate) - due 2026-03-09
Maya (Eng Manager) - confirm stakeholders for compliance sign-off if routing changes require SOC2 change - due 2026-03-08
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Okay thanks everyone for joining, uh this is the weekly POC sync, main focus today is the incident from last Thursday where you saw a spike in timeouts and some 5xxs during the big load run. We have Priya from our SE team here.
[00:18] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, yeah i pulled logs and we tried to correlate the 5xx bursts with resource pressure and a few routing changes, so i'll walk through what I saw. Apologies if transcription is messy, some names might be off.
[00:35] Maya (Aurora): thanks, quick context — we ran our simulated batch traffic from 10:30 to 11:15 and started seeing increased tail latency around 10:42 and errors ramped up at ~10:48, by 10:52 we hit rate limits and some of our clients saw 502/504s.
[01:05] Tom (Aurora SRE): yeah these looked like upstream timeouts mostly, some 500s that mapped to OOM kill on a pod in one availability zone but not all, i attached the pod logs in the ticket.
[01:28] Priya: i pulled the Redwood side traces — we see increased queueing, KV cache miss rate also rose, which pushed more compute per-request, and for a subset of requests the kernel-level tail latency spikes. so likely a mix of caching + scheduling.
[01:55] Victor (Data Eng): interesting, we did change our prompt size distribution for the test, average tokens per request doubled which may have amplified KV miss impact.
[02:10] Priya: that would explain it, larger generated sequences exacerbate kv cache pressure; our runtime does continuous batching and if batch sizes grow unpredictably that can increase peak memory usage.
[02:35] Alex: can you explain the rate limit behavior observed? we saw some 429s then rapid retries from the client which made the load pattern worse.
[02:46] Tom: yes, our client retried aggressively, we have exponential backoff but the jitter was small; when 429s hit at scale the retry storm made more requests hit the same buckets.
[03:02] Priya: for immediate mitigation we recommended increasing client-side jitter and adding a small random delay, and also temporarily routing critical routes to a dedicated pool where you have reserved capacity. that reduces the chance of noisy neighbors.
[03:20] Maya: how fast can routing change happen? we need it asap for the next test window.
[03:26] Alex: we can push a routing policy change in the control plane within an hour once we agree on the routes. priya will provide the exact route names.
[03:38] Priya: i'll send the route list in chat after the call. also we proposed tweaking retry policy (max attempts from 5 to 3 with increasing base backoff and jitter) to limit retry amplification.
[03:56] Tom: ok 3 attempts sounds fine; we'll change client too.
[04:02] Victor: on the 5xx classification — are these all service-level errors or some are downstream infra?
[04:09] Priya: mixed — we saw 502/504 from proxy timeouts, a handful of 500s due to pod restarts (OOM), and couple of kernel-level stalls that look like scheduling latency. we need more traces to pinpoint frequency.
[04:32] Alex: can you share the redwood logs for the windows? we need to see the sampled traces and kernel metrics.
[04:39] Priya: yes i'll filter and redact PII then upload.
[04:44] Maya: re: security/compliance, if we reroute to dedicated pool does that change our data residency or audit logs?
[04:53] Alex: no default data residency doesn't change; dedicated pool will just be reserved capacity in the same region, same control plane and audit logs, and we can provide a SOC2 note — i'll attach the SOC2 section.
[05:05] Lena (Product): any risk to model quality if we change quantization or run in a different instance type?
[05:12] Priya: for short term we won't change quantization; routing is to identical model variant on dedicated GPUs. long term we might recommend a different quant profile but that's after we stabilize.
[05:24] Tom: curious about kernel/runtime tuning — you mentioned possible kernel-level fixes, can we get a deeper session?
[05:31] Priya: yes if traces indicate kernel scheduling is dominant we can pull in our runtime/kernel team; likely tasks would be kernel flags, cgroup tuning, and batching thresholds. we'll only escalate if metrics support it.
[05:47] Alex: quick recap — immediate actions: Priya to upload logs/traces, Alex to propose routing change and retry policy, Aurora to run controlled staging test with script v2 and send results. then we reconvene after test.
[06:03] Victor: one more note — during the incident we saw a small spike in KV cache misses, what's the plan to improve hit rate?
[06:11] Priya: options are pre-warming cache for common prefixes, increasing cache size for pilot, or adjusting batching to keep more keys hot — i'll include hit-rate numbers in the upload.
[06:26] Maya: timeline wise we want mitigation in place before next production run on Monday.
[06:31] Alex: agreed. we'll aim to have mitigations staged by end of week.
[06:38] Lena: please include a short runbook for on-call SREs in case similar errors reoccur.
[06:44] Priya: yes we will produce an abbreviated runbook with thresholds and immediate steps (reduce client concurrency, switch routing, escalate to Redwood SE).
[06:55] Alex: ok any other questions?
[07:00] Tom: none from me, thanks.
[07:03] Maya: thanks team.
[07:05] Alex: thanks all, i'll follow up with the docs and the route list. bye.
notes: Transcript contains some minor transcription artifacts; technical content verified by Redwood SE after call. References to pods, KV cache, kernel-level stalls, and routing policies are best-effort phrasings from the live call.
